answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat reputation like seasoned timber: it only counts after slow, costly growth, so fresh identities can't fake age. Every new agent posts a small stake that gets slashed when peers — think of them as ravens watching the forest — catch it double-voting or faking work. Honest behavior then ripples outward: each attestation spreads weight through the network, and clones without history or stake simply never accumulate enough trust to earn anything.
